units.title: The data model & idioms for pipelines
units.text:
Everything in Python is an object with an identity, type and value; names are references, not boxes, which is why mutability bites (aliasing a list vs copying it). The data model is the dunder methods (__len__, __iter__, __getitem__, __repr__, __eq__, __hash__) that let YOUR objects behave like built-ins and plug into for, len(), slicing and in.
🎥 Watch: James Powell — 'So you want to be a Python expert?' (PyData); skim Fluent Python ch.1.
💻 Code: Build an immutable Record (with __repr__, __eq__, __hash__) and a Dataset collection implementing __iter__, __len__, __getitem__ so loops, len() and slicing all work.

units.title: Iterators, generators & streaming data
units.text:
A generator (yield) is the easy way to write an iterator, suspending state between values to give lazy, constant-memory streams — the core DE trick for a 10GB file that won't fit in RAM. Chain generators source -> filter -> transform -> sink and lean on itertools for batching and windowing.
🎥 Watch: David Beazley — 'Generator Tricks for Systems Programmers'.
💻 Code: Write a generator pipeline that streams a huge CSV line-by-line, filters and transforms lazily, and aggregates a metric; confirm flat memory with memory_profiler.

units.title: Typing, dataclasses & pydantic schemas
units.text:
Type hints unlock static checking; dataclasses give cheap internal records; pydantic adds runtime validation and coercion. At every pipeline boundary you want a schema that rejects bad data loudly instead of letting a null propagate three stages downstream.
🎥 Watch: mCoding — Python type hints; ArjanCodes — Pydantic tutorial.
💻 Code: Define a pydantic model for an input record (types, ranges, enums, a custom validator); feed it clean and dirty data and handle ValidationError without killing the batch.

units.title: Context managers & robust error handling
units.text:
The with protocol (__enter__/__exit__, or @contextmanager) guarantees cleanup even when the body raises. Pair it with custom exception types, catch-narrow-not-broad, and retry-with-backoff for flaky I/O so one bad row or network blip doesn't kill a run — this is what separates a script from a pipeline.
🎥 Watch: Corey Schafer — Context Managers; ArjanCodes — error-handling patterns.
💻 Code: Write a context manager that cleans up a resource on error plus a retry decorator with exponential backoff; prove the failure path works by injecting exceptions in a test.

units.title: Testing data code (pytest, fixtures)
units.text:
Data code is testable code: pytest fixtures for setup/teardown, parametrize for table-driven cases, mocking for external services, and hypothesis for property-based tests that generate edge cases (empty, unicode, huge, negative). Untested pipelines fail silently in production; tested ones fail in CI.
🎥 Watch: Corey Schafer — pytest; the Hypothesis 'Getting Started' docs/talk.
💻 Code: Write pytest tests + fixtures for your Record/Dataset and the CSV generator, add a parametrized case table, and one hypothesis property test (e.g. round-trip parse/serialize).

units.title: Typed, tested data-ingestion library
units.text: [Block A] Core: a generator-based reader that streams from CSV/JSON/an API, yielding validated pydantic records; lazy, constant memory, with a clean typed API ingest(source) -> Iterator[Record]. [Block B] Robustness: context-managed resources, a retry-with-backoff wrapper for the API source, structured logging, and a configurable errors policy (skip-and-log vs fail-fast). [Block C] Ship: a Typer CLI, a full pytest suite (+ one hypothesis test), pyproject.toml and a README, then push it to GitHub as your first portfolio repo of the plan.

units.title: Pythonic data code
units.text: The data model gives clean abstractions, generators give constant-memory streams, typing/pydantic guard your boundaries, context managers + retries give reliability, and pytest keeps it honest. Re-read your ingestion library and refactor one rough edge with fresh eyes.
units.mastery: Cold: how does a generator pipeline keep memory flat on a 10GB file, and exactly where in an ingestion flow do schema validation, retries and tests belong — and why there?

units.title: Concurrency: threads, processes, asyncio
units.text:
The GIL means threads help I/O-bound work, not CPU-bound; use multiprocessing for CPU, asyncio for thousands of concurrent I/O waits. The skill is matching the model to the bottleneck.
🎥 Watch: David Beazley — 'Python Concurrency From the Ground Up'; mCoding — asyncio.
💻 Code: Fetch 100 URLs three ways (threads, processes, asyncio), time each, and explain which wins and why.

units.title: Performance & vectorization
units.text:
Python loops are slow; push work into C via NumPy/pandas vectorization or batching, and always measure before optimizing.
🎥 Watch: Jake VanderPlas — 'Losing your Loops: Fast Numerical Computing with NumPy' (PyCon).
💻 Code: Rewrite a nested-loop numeric transform with NumPy vectorization and measure the speedup.

units.title: Profiling CPU & memory
units.text:
cProfile and py-spy find CPU hotspots; memory_profiler and tracemalloc find leaks. Optimize the top of the flat profile, not guesses.
🎥 Watch: mCoding — 'Python profiling'; search 'py-spy sampling profiler' (Ben Frederickson).
💻 Code: Profile a slow script with cProfile + py-spy, find the hotspot, and cut its runtime in half.

units.title: Packaging & CLIs (Typer)
units.text:
pyproject.toml, virtual envs and building distributable tools; Typer/Click turn scripts into clean CLIs with types, subcommands and help.
🎥 Watch: ArjanCodes — 'Python packaging'; the Typer docs tutorial.
💻 Code: Turn a script into an installable package with a Typer CLI (subcommands, --help, typed options).

units.title: Structured logging & configuration
units.text:
Logging over print (levels, handlers, structured/JSON logs), plus config via env/files (pydantic-settings). Observability starts here.
🎥 Watch: mCoding — 'Modern Python logging'.
💻 Code: Add structured JSON logging + env-based config to your Week-1 ingestion library.

units.title: Profile & optimize a slow pipeline 10x
units.text: [Block A] Take a deliberately slow data script (nested loops, per-row I/O, no batching) and profile it with cProfile + py-spy to find the real bottlenecks. [Block B] Optimize: vectorize the hot numeric path, batch the I/O, add concurrency where I/O-bound; re-measure after each change. [Block C] Write it up: a before/after benchmark table and a short note on what mattered and why — a clean 'performance engineering' portfolio post.

units.title: Fast, reliable Python
units.text: Concurrency model, vectorization, profiling, packaging and logging turn scripts into tools. Re-profile your optimized pipeline and confirm the win is real, not luck.
units.mastery: When do threads help and when do they hurt in Python, and what is your first move when a pipeline is 'too slow'?

units.title: Relational model & normalization
units.text:
Relations, keys and functional dependencies; normalize (1NF -> 3NF) to kill update anomalies, then denormalize deliberately for read speed.
🎥 Watch: CMU Intro to Database Systems (Andy Pavlo) — the relational model lecture.
💻 Code: Design a normalized schema for orders/customers/products in Postgres with keys and constraints.

units.title: SQL deep: window functions & CTEs
units.text:
Window functions (rank, lag, running totals) and CTEs (incl. recursive) are the tools that separate junior from senior SQL.
🎥 Watch: Mode SQL tutorial (window functions); search 'SQL window functions explained'.
💻 Code: Solve 5 analytical queries using windows + CTEs: running totals, top-N per group, sessionization.

units.title: Query planning & indexes (EXPLAIN)
units.text:
How the planner picks scans and joins, how B-tree indexes work, reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and when an index helps vs hurts.
🎥 Watch: Hussein Nasser — database indexing / EXPLAIN; 'Use The Index, Luke' (Markus Winand).
💻 Code: Take a slow query, read EXPLAIN ANALYZE, add the right index, and show the plan change + speedup.

units.title: Transactions, ACID & isolation levels
units.text:
ACID and isolation levels (read committed -> serializable) and the anomalies each prevents: dirty, non-repeatable and phantom reads; locking vs MVCC.
🎥 Watch: CMU Pavlo — concurrency control; Hussein Nasser — isolation levels.
💻 Code: Reproduce a lost-update / non-repeatable-read anomaly in Postgres, then fix it by raising the isolation level.

units.title: Postgres internals: MVCC, WAL, vacuum
units.text:
How Postgres does MVCC (tuple versions, xmin/xmax), the WAL for durability and crash recovery, and why VACUUM and bloat matter in practice.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Postgres MVCC explained' (Hussein Nasser) and 'Postgres WAL'.
💻 Code: Inspect tuple visibility (xmin/xmax) with pageinspect, watch table bloat grow, then run VACUUM.

units.title: Schema design + a 100x query optimization
units.text: [Block A] Design and load a realistic schema (a few million rows) — orders, users, events — with proper keys and constraints. [Block B] Find the 5 slowest analytical queries, read their plans, and optimize with indexes, rewrites and (where apt) materialized views — target 100x on at least one. [Block C] Document the before/after plans and numbers as a 'SQL performance' portfolio writeup.

units.title: How a database thinks
units.text: The relational model, SQL power features, the planner + indexes, transactions and MVCC together explain how a DB stays fast and correct. Re-run your optimizations and reread the plans.
units.mastery: Walk through what happens from EXPLAIN to result for a slow join, and how MVCC lets readers not block writers.

units.title: Storage engines: B-tree vs LSM-tree
units.text:
B-trees are read-optimized and update in place; LSM-trees are write-optimized (memtable + SSTables + compaction). This is why Postgres and Cassandra/RocksDB chose differently.
🎥 Watch: DDIA ch.3 concepts; CMU Pavlo — storage / tree indexes; 'LSM tree vs B-tree'.
💻 Code: Sketch a toy LSM: an in-memory memtable that flushes sorted runs to disk, with a simple read-merge.

units.title: Columnar stores; OLTP vs OLAP
units.text:
Row stores serve transactions; column stores serve analytics via compression, vectorized scans and predicate pushdown — which is why your warehouse is columnar.
🎥 Watch: CMU Pavlo — column stores; search 'columnar databases explained'.
💻 Code: Compare speed + size of the same aggregation as row (Postgres) vs columnar (DuckDB/Parquet).

units.title: The NoSQL landscape
units.text:
KV, document, wide-column and graph stores — what each is good and bad at, and when NOT to reach for them.
🎥 Watch: Hussein Nasser — 'NoSQL explained'; DDIA ch.2.
💻 Code: Model the same domain in a KV, a document and a relational store; note what each makes easy or hard.

units.title: Caching (Redis) & serialization
units.text:
Redis data structures and cache patterns (cache-aside, TTLs, and the hard part — invalidation); serialization format tradeoffs.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Redis crash course' (Web Dev Simplified / Hussein Nasser).
💻 Code: Add a cache-aside layer (Redis) in front of a slow query; measure hit-rate and latency.

units.title: File formats: Parquet, Avro, ORC, Protobuf
units.text:
Parquet/ORC are columnar (encoding, compression, footers, predicate pushdown); Avro/Protobuf are row-oriented with schemas. These are what your lakehouse lives on.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Apache Parquet file format explained' and 'Avro vs Parquet'.
💻 Code: Write a dataset to CSV vs Parquet; compare size and read a single column with pushdown — measure the win.

units.title: Mini LSM-tree storage engine
units.text: [Block A] Core: a memtable (sorted in-memory) that flushes to immutable on-disk SSTables when full; put/get/delete. [Block B] Reads + compaction: the read path merges memtable + SSTables newest-first (tombstones for deletes); a compaction that merges SSTables and drops dead keys. [Block C] Benchmark it vs a dict and vs SQLite; write up write-amplification and read-path tradeoffs — a standout systems portfolio project.
units.demo: Write-optimized LSM-tree storage engine (memtable, SSTables, compaction) built from scratch.

units.title: Storage & serialization
units.text: Storage engines, columnar vs row, the NoSQL menu, caching and file formats are the physical layer under every pipeline. Re-read your LSM and note where a real engine adds a bloom filter or a WAL.
units.mastery: Why is an LSM-tree write-optimized and a B-tree read-optimized, and why is Parquet the right default for analytics?

units.title: Reliability, scalability, maintainability
units.text:
The three concerns of data-intensive systems; measure load and latency with percentiles (not averages), and design for failure as the normal case.
🎥 Watch: Martin Kleppmann — DDIA; his 'Distributed Systems' lecture 1 (Cambridge, on YouTube).
💻 Code: Instrument a service to record p50/p95/p99 latency under load; explain why the average lied.

units.title: Data models & query languages
units.text:
Relational vs document vs graph models and their query languages, the impedance mismatch, and when each fits.
🎥 Watch: DDIA ch.2; Kleppmann — data models lecture.
💻 Code: Model a many-to-many domain relationally and as documents; write 'friends-of-friends' in each and compare pain.

units.title: Replication: leaders, followers, lag
units.text:
Single-leader replication, sync vs async, replication lag, and read-your-writes — why a follower can serve stale reads.
🎥 Watch: DDIA ch.5; Kleppmann — replication lectures.
💻 Code: Simulate leader -> follower with artificial lag; demonstrate a stale read and a read-your-writes fix.

units.title: Partitioning & sharding
units.text:
Partitioning by key range vs hash, hot spots, rebalancing, and routing a request to the right shard.
🎥 Watch: DDIA ch.6; Kleppmann — partitioning lecture.
💻 Code: Build a hash-partitioned KV over N nodes; show a hot-key problem and mitigate it.

units.title: CAP & consistency models
units.text:
CAP (really PACELC), linearizability vs eventual consistency, and why 'consistency' means different things to a DBA and to CAP.
🎥 Watch: Kleppmann — 'Please stop calling databases CP or AP'; DDIA ch.9 concepts.
💻 Code: Demonstrate eventual consistency: concurrent writes to replicas converging (or not) under different rules.

units.title: Sharded KV store with a replication-lag sim
units.text: [Block A] Build a hash-sharded in-memory KV across N simulated nodes with a client-side router. [Block B] Add single-leader replication per shard with configurable async lag; expose read-from-leader vs read-from-follower. [Block C] A test harness that shows stale reads under lag and read-your-writes when reading the leader; document the tradeoffs.

units.title: Why distributed is hard
units.text: Reliability metrics, data models, replication, partitioning and consistency are the vocabulary of every distributed data system. Re-read DDIA's chapter summaries for the week.
units.mastery: Explain replication lag with a concrete read-your-writes bug, and why partitioning creates hot spots.

units.title: Consensus: Raft & Paxos intuition
units.text:
Why consensus is needed (agree on a value despite failures), Raft's leader election and log replication, and Paxos at a high level.
🎥 Watch: MIT 6.824 — Raft lectures (Robert Morris); the Raft paper + the raft.github.io visualization.
💻 Code: Implement Raft leader election (terms, votes, election timeouts) for a 3-node cluster.

units.title: Distributed transactions: 2PC & saga
units.text:
Two-phase commit and its blocking problem; the saga pattern with compensating actions for long-lived business transactions.
🎥 Watch: DDIA ch.9; Hussein Nasser — 'saga pattern'.
💻 Code: Implement a saga for a 3-step booking with compensation when any step fails.

units.title: Event ordering & exactly-once
units.text:
Logical clocks (Lamport, vector), idempotency, and why 'exactly-once' is really at-least-once + idempotent processing.
🎥 Watch: Kleppmann — logical clocks; search 'exactly once semantics Kafka'.
💻 Code: Make a non-idempotent consumer idempotent with a dedup key so replays don't double-count.

units.title: Fault tolerance & failure modes
units.text:
Partial failure, timeouts, retries with backoff + jitter, circuit breakers, and the fallacies of distributed computing.
🎥 Watch: Search 'fallacies of distributed computing' and resilience-pattern talks.
💻 Code: Add timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and a circuit breaker to a flaky client.

units.title: Batch vs stream paradigms
units.text:
Bounded (batch) vs unbounded (stream) processing and how they converge (the Dataflow model) — the bridge to the streaming weeks.
🎥 Watch: Tyler Akidau — 'The world beyond batch: Streaming 101/102'.
💻 Code: Compute a daily aggregate two ways — as a batch job and as an incremental stream — and compare.

units.title: Mini distributed log (Raft-lite)
units.text: [Block A] Build a replicated append-only log across 3 nodes with Raft leader election and log replication (append, commit index). [Block B] Handle failure: leader crash -> re-election -> the new leader preserves the committed prefix consistently. [Block C] Add a tiny KV state machine on top (the log is the source of truth) and test linearizable reads — a flagship systems portfolio project.
units.demo: Raft consensus — leader election + replicated log with crash recovery, from scratch.

units.title: Coordination & correctness
units.text: Consensus, distributed transactions, ordering/idempotency, fault tolerance and the batch/stream split are the hard core of distributed data. Re-read your Raft-lite and find its remaining edge cases.
units.mastery: How does Raft keep a consistent committed log across a leader crash, and why is 'exactly-once' really idempotency?

units.title: Star schema: facts & dimensions
units.text:
The star schema — a central fact table of measurements surrounded by descriptive dimensions — is the analytics default because it maps to how people ask questions.
🎥 Watch: Kimball Group resources; search 'star schema / dimensional modeling explained'.
💻 Code: Model a retail-sales star (fact_sales + dim_date/product/store/customer) in SQL/dbt.

units.title: Grain & additivity
units.text:
Declare the grain first (one row per what?); classify measures as additive, semi-additive (can't sum across time, e.g. a balance) or non-additive (ratios).
🎥 Watch: The Data Warehouse Toolkit (Kimball) ch.1-2 concepts.
💻 Code: Pick a grain for an events fact and label every measure additive / semi / non-additive.

units.title: Slowly changing dimensions (SCD 1/2/3)
units.text:
Handling dimension change over time: overwrite (type 1), add a versioned row (type 2), add a column (type 3). SCD2 is the workhorse for 'what was true then?'.
🎥 Watch: Search 'slowly changing dimensions type 2 explained'.
💻 Code: Implement an SCD2 dimension (effective_from/to, is_current) with a merge that versions changes.

units.title: Conformed dimensions & the bus matrix
units.text:
Shared 'conformed' dimensions let facts from different processes be compared; the Kimball bus matrix is the plan that keeps them conformed.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Kimball bus matrix conformed dimensions'.
💻 Code: Draw a bus matrix for 3 business processes and identify the conformed dimensions.

units.title: Data Vault & OBT tradeoffs
units.text:
When to use Kimball vs Data Vault (hubs/links/satellites) vs One Big Table (wide, columnar-friendly) — modern warehouse pragmatism.
🎥 Watch: Search 'data vault vs kimball' and 'one big table modern data stack'.
💻 Code: Model the same domain as a star and as an OBT; note the query and maintenance tradeoffs.

units.title: Model a real domain into a star schema + dbt
units.text: [Block A] Pick a real domain (rides, e-commerce, or your own data) and design the star: declare grain, facts and conformed dimensions. [Block B] Implement it in dbt on a warehouse: staging -> dimension models (including one SCD2) -> fact models, with tests. [Block C] Add docs + a bus matrix and a couple of analytical queries; ship as a dbt portfolio repo.

units.title: Modeling for analytics
units.text: Grain, facts/dimensions, SCDs, conformed dimensions and the Kimball-vs-Vault-vs-OBT choice are how raw data becomes analyzable. Review your star for grain mistakes.
units.mastery: Why declare the grain first, and how does an SCD2 dimension let you answer 'what was true at the time'?

units.title: Modern warehouse architecture
units.text:
Separation of storage and compute (Snowflake/BigQuery/Redshift), MPP execution, and why the cloud warehouse reshaped data teams.
🎥 Watch: Search 'how Snowflake works architecture' and 'BigQuery Dremel architecture'.
💻 Code: Load a dataset into a cloud warehouse (or DuckDB as a stand-in) and inspect how it stores and scans.

units.title: Partitioning, clustering & distribution
units.text:
The physical-layout knobs — partitioning, clustering/sort keys, distribution — that make scans cheap.
🎥 Watch: Search '<your warehouse> clustering and partitioning best practices'.
💻 Code: Partition + cluster a large table on the right columns; measure bytes scanned before vs after.

units.title: Warehouse query optimization
units.text:
Partition pruning, avoiding data movement (shuffles), spilling, and reading a warehouse query profile.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Snowflake query profile' or 'BigQuery query plan explained'.
💻 Code: Optimize an expensive warehouse query using its profile; cut the bytes scanned.

units.title: Cost & performance tuning
units.text:
Warehouses bill for compute and scan — sizing, auto-suspend, materialization and cost observability. FinOps for data.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Snowflake cost optimization' or 'BigQuery cost control'.
💻 Code: Find your 3 most expensive queries and cut their cost via materialization, pruning or right-sizing.

units.title: Semantic layers & metrics
units.text:
Define each metric once, in a semantic/metrics layer, so every tool agrees — the cure for 'why are our two dashboards different?'.
🎥 Watch: Search 'semantic layer explained'; dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow docs.
💻 Code: Define 2-3 core business metrics in a semantic layer and query them consistently.

units.title: dbt warehouse: staging to marts, tests, docs
units.text: [Block A] Set up dbt on a warehouse (or DuckDB): sources + staging models with tests (not_null, unique, relationships). [Block B] Build mart models (the dims + facts from Week 7), incremental where apt, and add a metrics/semantic layer. [Block C] Generate docs + lineage, wire a CI check, and publish — a complete analytics-engineering portfolio piece.

units.title: The warehouse as a product
units.text: Architecture, physical layout, query and cost tuning and a semantic layer turn a warehouse into a reliable product. Review your cost wins.
units.mastery: How does separating storage and compute change how you tune, and why does a semantic layer prevent metric drift?

units.title: Architecture: driver, executors, managers
units.text:
The driver plans, executors do the work, a cluster manager (YARN/K8s/standalone) allocates resources; a job splits into stages at shuffle boundaries, stages into tasks.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark architecture explained' (Data Savvy / Learning Journal); Spark: The Definitive Guide ch.2-3.
💻 Code: Run a Spark job locally and read the Spark UI: trace jobs -> stages -> tasks.

units.title: RDDs, the DAG & lazy evaluation
units.text:
RDDs are the low-level abstraction; transformations are lazy, actions trigger execution, and the scheduler builds a DAG of the work.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark RDD DAG lazy evaluation'.
💻 Code: Chain several transformations then one action; observe nothing runs until the action, and read the DAG.

units.title: Catalyst optimizer & Tungsten
units.text:
The DataFrame API compiles through Catalyst (logical -> optimized -> physical plan) and Tungsten optimizes memory and codegen — why DataFrames beat raw RDDs.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark Catalyst optimizer explained'; Databricks deep-dive talks.
💻 Code: Call explain() on a DataFrame query; find predicate pushdown and read the physical plan.

units.title: DataFrames vs Datasets vs SQL
units.text:
The three structured APIs, when to use each, and why Python users live in DataFrames/SQL (no compile-time Dataset types).
🎥 Watch: Spark: The Definitive Guide — Structured APIs.
💻 Code: Express the same transformation in the DataFrame API and in Spark SQL; confirm identical plans.

units.title: Partitions, shuffles, wide vs narrow deps
units.text:
Narrow dependencies (map/filter) stay local; wide dependencies (groupBy/join) force a shuffle — the expensive stage boundary.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark shuffle explained wide narrow dependencies'.
💻 Code: Trigger a shuffle with groupBy; read the stage boundary and shuffle read/write in the UI.

units.title: Analyze a large dataset; read the query plans
units.text: [Block A] Load a multi-GB dataset (e.g. NYC taxi) and write several analytical DataFrame/SQL queries. [Block B] For each, read explain() and the Spark UI — identify shuffles, stage boundaries and any skew. [Block C] Write up 'how Spark ran my query': the DAG, stages, shuffles and one thing you would tune.

units.title: How Spark executes
units.text: Driver/executors, RDDs + the DAG, Catalyst/Tungsten, the API choices and shuffles explain every Spark job. Re-read one of your query plans.
units.mastery: Trace a groupBy from code to physical plan to tasks — where does the shuffle happen and why is it costly?

units.title: Memory management: execution/storage & spill
units.text:
Executor memory splits into execution (shuffles/joins/sorts) and storage (cache); when it runs out Spark spills to disk — the silent killer of job speed.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark memory management explained'; Databricks tuning talks.
💻 Code: Cache a DataFrame and watch storage memory in the UI, then force a spill and observe the slowdown.

units.title: Joins: broadcast, sort-merge, skew & AQE
units.text:
Broadcast small tables, sort-merge large ones; data skew makes one task run forever. Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) fixes many join problems at runtime.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark join strategies skew AQE'.
💻 Code: Force a broadcast join, cause a skewed sort-merge join, then enable AQE + salting and measure the fix.

units.title: PySpark: UDFs, pandas UDFs, Arrow
units.text:
Plain Python UDFs are slow (per-row serialization); pandas/vectorized UDFs with Arrow are far faster — prefer built-ins, then pandas UDFs, then plain UDFs last.
🎥 Watch: Search 'PySpark pandas UDF Arrow performance'.
💻 Code: Implement one transform as a plain UDF and as a pandas UDF; benchmark the difference.

units.title: Performance tuning: partitioning & caching
units.text:
Right-size partitions (avoid tiny or huge), repartition vs coalesce, cache what you reuse, and tune shuffle partitions.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark performance tuning partitions shuffle'.
💻 Code: Fix an over-partitioned job (200k tiny tasks) and an under-partitioned one; measure both.

units.title: Debugging via the Spark UI
units.text:
The Spark UI is your distributed debugger: long stages, skew (one slow task), spills, GC and shuffle sizes all show up there.
🎥 Watch: Search 'reading the Spark UI'; Databricks 'Spark UI' talks.
💻 Code: Take a slow job, diagnose the bottleneck purely from the Spark UI, and prove your fix.

units.title: Optimize a Spark job 10x / fix a skewed join
units.text: [Block A] Start from a deliberately slow Spark job (skewed join, bad partitioning, Python UDFs) on a real dataset. [Block B] Diagnose from the Spark UI and fix: broadcast/salt the join, right-size partitions, vectorize UDFs, enable AQE — measure at each step. [Block C] Portfolio writeup: Spark UI screenshots, each fix, and the 10x before/after.

units.title: Making Spark fast
units.text: Memory/spill, join strategies + skew, UDF choices, partitioning and UI-driven debugging turn a crawling Spark job into a fast one. Re-open your tuned job's UI.
units.mastery: Given one task running 10x longer than the rest, what is happening and what are your three fixes?

units.title: Lakehouse architecture & Databricks
units.text:
The lakehouse merges the lake's cheap open storage with the warehouse's transactions and performance; Databricks is the managed platform around it.
🎥 Watch: Search 'lakehouse architecture explained'; a Databricks Lakehouse keynote.
💻 Code: Spin up a free Databricks workspace and run a notebook over a Delta table.

units.title: Delta Lake internals: log & time travel
units.text:
Delta adds an ordered transaction log (_delta_log JSON + checkpoints) over Parquet, giving ACID, time travel and schema enforcement on a lake.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Delta Lake transaction log explained'; Databricks Delta deep dives.
💻 Code: Make several writes to a Delta table, inspect _delta_log, and query an older version with time travel.

units.title: Delta vs Iceberg vs Hudi
units.text:
The three open table formats — how each handles metadata, snapshots and partitioning — and how to choose (engine support, ecosystem).
🎥 Watch: Search 'Delta vs Iceberg vs Hudi comparison'.
💻 Code: Create the same table in Delta and Iceberg; compare their metadata layout.

units.title: Medallion: bronze / silver / gold
units.text:
The bronze (raw) -> silver (cleaned/conformed) -> gold (business-ready) pattern for organizing a lakehouse.
🎥 Watch: Search 'medallion architecture bronze silver gold'.
💻 Code: Build a 3-layer medallion flow for one dataset in Delta.

units.title: Unity Catalog, Photon & governance
units.text:
Governance (catalogs, lineage, access control) via Unity Catalog, and the Photon vectorized engine for speed.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Databricks Unity Catalog' and 'Photon engine'.
💻 Code: Register tables in a catalog, set a grant, and view lineage.

units.title: Medallion lakehouse on Databricks (Delta + DLT)
units.text: [Block A] Ingest a raw source into a bronze Delta table (batch or streaming). [Block B] Build silver (validated, deduped, SCD where apt) and gold (aggregated marts) with Delta Live Tables or notebooks + tests. [Block C] Add data-quality expectations, a time-travel demo and lineage; publish as a lakehouse portfolio project.
units.demo: Medallion lakehouse on Databricks with Delta Lake (bronze/silver/gold, DLT, time travel).

units.title: The lakehouse paradigm
units.text: The transaction log, table-format choices, the medallion pattern and governance turn a pile of Parquet into a real platform. Re-inspect your _delta_log.
units.mastery: How does the Delta transaction log give you ACID + time travel on top of immutable Parquet files?

units.title: Kafka architecture: topics, partitions, offsets
units.text:
Kafka is a distributed, partitioned, replicated commit log; a topic splits into ordered partitions, each message has an offset — the unit of parallelism and ordering.
🎥 Watch: Confluent — Apache Kafka 101; Kafka: The Definitive Guide ch.1-2.
💻 Code: Run Kafka locally, create a topic with N partitions, produce/consume, and watch offsets advance.

units.title: Producers, consumers & consumer groups
units.text:
Producers pick partitions by key hashing; consumer groups split partitions across members for scale-out, rebalancing on join/leave.
🎥 Watch: Confluent — producers/consumers; 'Kafka consumer groups explained'.
💻 Code: Run 2 consumers in a group over a 4-partition topic; add a third and watch rebalancing.

units.title: Delivery semantics & idempotence
units.text:
At-most / at-least / exactly-once; the idempotent producer and transactions, and why consumers still need idempotent processing.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Kafka exactly once semantics'.
💻 Code: Show duplicate delivery on retry, then make the consumer idempotent with a dedup store.

units.title: Internals: the log, ISR, retention, compaction
units.text:
The segmented on-disk log (page-cache friendly), in-sync replicas (ISR) for durability, and retention vs log compaction.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Kafka internals log segments ISR compaction'.
💻 Code: Configure retention + a compacted topic; observe old records expire vs latest-per-key kept.

units.title: Schema Registry & Kafka Connect
units.text:
Schema Registry (Avro/Protobuf/JSON schema) for safe evolution, and Kafka Connect for source/sink integration without code.
🎥 Watch: Confluent — Schema Registry and Kafka Connect.
💻 Code: Register an Avro schema, produce with it, evolve it compatibly, and sink to a store via Connect.

units.title: Real-time pipeline: producer to Kafka to sink
units.text: [Block A] Build a producer that streams events (clicks/txns) into a partitioned topic with keys + an Avro schema. [Block B] A consumer group that processes and writes to a sink (Postgres/Delta), idempotently. [Block C] Add monitoring (lag, throughput) and a load test; document the ordering + delivery guarantees.

units.title: Logs as the backbone
units.text: Topics/partitions/offsets, consumer groups, delivery semantics, the on-disk log and Schema Registry/Connect make Kafka the nervous system of streaming data. Re-check your consumer lag.
units.mastery: How do partitions give both ordering and parallelism, and why is 'exactly-once' really idempotent consumption?

units.title: Windows, watermarks & state
units.text:
Stream processing needs windows (tumbling/sliding/session), watermarks to bound late data, and managed state — the model behind every engine.
🎥 Watch: Tyler Akidau — Streaming 101/102; Flink docs on time & windows.
💻 Code: Compute a 5-minute tumbling count over a stream with a watermark for late events.

units.title: Spark Structured Streaming
units.text:
The 'stream as an unbounded table' model, triggers, output modes (append/update/complete), and checkpointing for exactly-once.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark Structured Streaming tutorial'; Databricks docs.
💻 Code: Read a Kafka stream in Structured Streaming, aggregate a windowed metric, write to Delta with checkpointing.

units.title: Flink concepts & comparison
units.text:
Flink's true-streaming, event-time and stateful model vs Spark's micro-batch — when each fits.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Flink vs Spark Structured Streaming'.
💻 Code: Sketch the same windowed job in Flink's model; note the event-time/state differences.

units.title: Event time vs processing time, late data
units.text:
Event-time (when it happened) vs processing-time (when seen); watermarks + allowed lateness decide when a window closes and how late data is handled.
🎥 Watch: Tyler Akidau — Streaming 102 (event time).
💻 Code: Inject out-of-order/late events and show how the watermark + allowed-lateness change results.

units.title: Streaming joins & aggregations
units.text:
Stream-stream joins (state + time bounds), stream-static joins, and stateful aggregations — the hard, stateful part.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Spark structured streaming joins'.
💻 Code: Join two streams within a time window (impressions to clicks) and emit the matched pairs.

units.title: Streaming analytics: Kafka to Structured Streaming to Delta
units.text: [Block A] Consume the Week-12 event stream with Structured Streaming; parse + validate. [Block B] Compute windowed, watermarked aggregations with checkpointed state; handle late data explicitly. [Block C] Write results to a gold Delta table and a tiny live view; document exactly-once + recovery. A flagship streaming project.
units.demo: Exactly-once streaming pipeline: Kafka → Spark Structured Streaming → Delta.

units.title: Thinking in streams
units.text: Windows, watermarks, state, event-time and streaming joins are a genuinely different mental model from batch. Re-read your watermark handling.
units.mastery: Why is event-time processing harder than processing-time, and what does a watermark actually decide?

units.title: DAGs, idempotency & backfills
units.text:
Pipelines as DAGs of tasks; idempotent, retryable tasks and backfilling partitioned history are what make schedules reliable.
🎥 Watch: Marc Lamberti — Airflow fundamentals; search 'idempotent data pipelines'.
💻 Code: Design a small DAG on paper: tasks, dependencies, and what makes each idempotent.

units.title: Airflow deep: operators, XComs, scheduling
units.text:
Operators, the scheduler + executor, XComs for small data passing, sensors, and schedule_interval/catchup.
🎥 Watch: Marc Lamberti — Airflow course; the Airflow docs.
💻 Code: Build a real Airflow DAG (extract -> transform -> load) with retries and a sensor.

units.title: Dagster assets / Prefect
units.text:
Asset-based orchestration (Dagster software-defined assets) and Prefect's Pythonic flows — a more data-aware model than task-only DAGs.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Dagster software-defined assets'; the Dagster docs.
💻 Code: Re-express the same pipeline as Dagster assets and compare to the Airflow DAG.

units.title: Pipeline patterns: incremental & CDC
units.text:
Incremental loads (high-water-mark), CDC-driven pipelines, and idempotent upserts/merges.
🎥 Watch: Search 'incremental data pipeline patterns'.
💻 Code: Convert a full-refresh load to incremental with a high-water-mark and an idempotent merge.

units.title: Observability & data SLAs
units.text:
Freshness/volume/latency SLAs, alerting on failure and lateness, and lineage for impact analysis.
🎥 Watch: Search 'data observability SLAs'.
💻 Code: Add task-level alerting + a freshness check to your DAG.

units.title: End-to-end orchestrated pipeline (Airflow/Dagster)
units.text: [Block A] Orchestrate a full flow — ingest -> warehouse/lakehouse transform (your dbt project) -> quality checks — as a DAG/asset graph. [Block B] Make it incremental + idempotent with retries, backfills and sensors on upstream data. [Block C] Add observability (freshness, alerting) and docs; a strong orchestration portfolio piece.

units.title: Reliable pipelines
units.text: DAGs + idempotency, Airflow/Dagster, incremental patterns and SLAs turn scripts-on-cron into dependable production pipelines. Trigger a backfill on your DAG.
units.mastery: Why must pipeline tasks be idempotent, and how does a high-water-mark make an incremental load safe to re-run?

units.title: dbt fundamentals: models, refs, sources
units.text:
dbt turns SQL SELECTs into a DAG of models with ref()/source() and materializations (view/table/incremental), compiled and run against your warehouse.
🎥 Watch: dbt Labs — 'dbt Fundamentals' (free course).
💻 Code: Init a dbt project, define sources + a few staging models with ref(), and run it.

units.title: Tests, docs & exposures
units.text:
Built-in + custom tests (not_null, unique, relationships, accepted_values), auto-docs, and exposures that track downstream use.
🎥 Watch: dbt Fundamentals — testing & docs.
💻 Code: Add schema + data tests to your models and generate the docs site.

units.title: Incremental models & snapshots
units.text:
Incremental materialization for big tables (process only new rows) and snapshots for SCD2 history capture.
🎥 Watch: Search 'dbt incremental models' and 'dbt snapshots'.
💻 Code: Convert a model to incremental and add a snapshot to track a dimension's history.

units.title: Macros, packages & Jinja
units.text:
Jinja templating, reusable macros and packages (dbt-utils) for DRY, testable SQL.
🎥 Watch: Search 'dbt macros jinja tutorial'.
💻 Code: Write a macro (e.g. a generic surrogate key) and pull in dbt-utils.

units.title: dbt in production: CI & environments
units.text:
dev/prod targets, slim CI (build only changed models), and deploying with a scheduler — the analytics-engineering workflow.
🎥 Watch: Search 'dbt slim CI'; dbt deployment docs.
💻 Code: Wire a CI check that builds + tests changed models on a PR.

units.title: Full analytics-engineering project (dbt)
units.text: [Block A] Build a complete dbt project: sources -> staging -> marts (dims + facts), with tests everywhere. [Block B] Add incremental models, a snapshot, custom macros and dbt-utils; generate docs + lineage. [Block C] Set up CI + environments and publish the repo — a portfolio-grade analytics-engineering project.

units.title: The analytics-engineering mindset
units.text: Models + refs, tests + docs, incremental/snapshots, macros and CI are software engineering applied to SQL. Re-read your DAG's lineage.
units.mastery: How does dbt's ref() build a DAG, and when do you reach for an incremental model vs a snapshot?

units.title: DQ dimensions & testing (Great Expectations)
units.text:
Quality dimensions (completeness, validity, uniqueness, freshness, consistency) codified as executable expectations.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Great Expectations tutorial'; the GX docs.
💻 Code: Add a Great Expectations suite (types, ranges, null rates) to a dataset and run it in the pipeline.

units.title: Data contracts & schema evolution
units.text:
Data contracts as a producer/consumer agreement, and safe schema evolution (backward/forward compatibility).
🎥 Watch: Search 'data contracts explained'.
💻 Code: Write a data contract (schema + SLAs) for a source and add a CI check that fails on breaking changes.

units.title: Lineage & catalogs
units.text:
Column/table lineage for impact analysis, and a data catalog for discovery/ownership (OpenMetadata/DataHub/Unity).
🎥 Watch: Search 'data lineage' and 'data catalog OpenMetadata DataHub'.
💻 Code: Generate lineage for your pipeline and register datasets with owners in a catalog.

units.title: Governance, PII & GDPR
units.text:
Classifying/masking PII, access control, and privacy regs (GDPR right-to-erasure) applied to a warehouse/lakehouse.
🎥 Watch: Search 'data governance PII masking'; GDPR-for-engineers overviews.
💻 Code: Tag PII columns, add masking for a role, and implement a delete-by-subject flow.

units.title: Observability: freshness, volume, schema
units.text:
Automated monitors for freshness, volume/row-count anomalies and schema drift — catching breakage before consumers do.
🎥 Watch: Search 'data observability freshness volume schema' (Monte Carlo concepts).
💻 Code: Add freshness + volume + schema-drift monitors with alerting to your pipeline.

units.title: Add data quality + lineage to a pipeline
units.text: [Block A] Instrument your orchestrated pipeline with Great Expectations checks at each layer (bronze/silver/gold). [Block B] Add a data contract + CI gate on the source, and freshness/volume/schema monitors with alerting. [Block C] Generate end-to-end lineage and register everything in a catalog; document the DQ strategy.

units.title: Trustworthy data
units.text: Expectations, contracts, lineage, governance and observability are how data earns trust. Break your source schema and watch the contract catch it.
units.mastery: Name the quality dimensions you'd monitor for a critical table, and how a data contract prevents silent breakage.

units.title: S3, Glue, Athena, EMR
units.text:
S3 as the data lake (storage classes, partitioned prefixes), Glue for catalog + ETL, Athena for serverless SQL, EMR for managed Spark.
🎥 Watch: Search 'AWS data lake S3 Glue Athena tutorial'.
💻 Code: Land partitioned Parquet in S3, crawl it with Glue, and query it with Athena.

units.title: Kinesis & Lambda for data
units.text:
Kinesis for streaming ingest and Lambda for event-driven serverless processing — when serverless beats a cluster.
🎥 Watch: Search 'AWS Kinesis Lambda data pipeline'.
💻 Code: Build a Kinesis -> Lambda -> S3 mini streaming ingest.

units.title: Redshift + IAM & cost
units.text:
Redshift architecture (distribution/sort keys, Spectrum), IAM for data access, and cloud cost control.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Redshift architecture distribution sort keys'.
💻 Code: Load data into Redshift Serverless, tune a query with dist/sort keys, and estimate cost.

units.title: CDC & log-based ingestion
units.text:
Change Data Capture with Debezium reading the DB WAL/binlog into Kafka — low-latency, low-load replication of changes.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Debezium CDC tutorial'; Confluent CDC talks.
💻 Code: Set up Debezium on Postgres, stream changes into Kafka, and materialize them in a sink.

units.title: Lambda vs Kappa; reverse ETL
units.text:
Lambda (batch + speed layers) vs Kappa (stream-only) architectures, and reverse ETL to push warehouse data into operational tools.
🎥 Watch: Search 'lambda vs kappa architecture' and 'reverse ETL explained'.
💻 Code: Diagram your platform as Kappa; sketch a reverse-ETL sync of a gold table to an app.

units.title: Serverless data pipeline (S3 + Glue + Athena)
units.text: [Block A] Ingest raw data to S3 (partitioned), catalog with Glue, transform with a Glue/Spark job to Parquet. [Block B] Expose it via Athena with partition pruning; add a Kinesis -> Lambda path for near-real-time. [Block C] Add least-privilege IAM, cost estimates and a preview of IaC; document the serverless design.

units.title: DE in the cloud
units.text: S3/Glue/Athena/EMR, Kinesis/Lambda, Redshift, CDC and the Lambda/Kappa choice are the cloud toolkit that ties the phase together. Review your IAM + cost.
units.mastery: When do you pick serverless (Athena/Lambda) over a cluster (EMR/Redshift), and what does CDC buy you over batch pulls?

units.title: Design the platform & data contracts
units.text:
Scope a real end-to-end platform: sources, SLAs, the medallion layers, and data contracts at the boundaries.
🎥 Watch: Revisit DDIA ch.1 and your Kimball/dbt notes as design references.
💻 Code: Write the design doc: an architecture diagram, the data contracts, and the SLAs you'll hit.

units.title: Ingestion & the bronze layer
units.text:
Batch + streaming ingestion into raw/bronze with schema capture and idempotent, replay-safe landing.
🎥 Watch: Reuse your Kafka + ingestion-library patterns.
💻 Code: Build ingestion into bronze (Kafka/CDC + batch) with validation and replay-safety.

units.title: Transformation & modeling (silver/gold)
units.text:
Clean/conform to silver and model business marts (dims + facts, SCD2) to gold with dbt on your lakehouse/warehouse.
🎥 Watch: Reuse your dbt + dimensional-modeling work.
💻 Code: Build silver + gold with dbt: staging, dims (incl. SCD2), facts, tests.

units.title: Orchestration, quality & monitoring
units.text:
Orchestrate the flow (Airflow/Dagster), add DQ (Great Expectations) and observability (freshness/volume) end to end.
🎥 Watch: Reuse your orchestration + DQ patterns.
💻 Code: Wire the whole DAG with retries/backfills, quality gates and alerting.

units.title: Ship, document & diagram
units.text:
Package, write the README/architecture doc, add lineage, and prepare the portfolio narrative.
🎥 Watch: Study a couple of strong data-platform case studies for structure.
💻 Code: Finalize docs + lineage + a diagram and record a short walkthrough.

units.title: Data-platform capstone — build & ship
units.text: [Block A] Assemble the full platform: ingest (batch + streaming/CDC) -> bronze -> silver -> gold, orchestrated. [Block B] Add data quality, observability and cost/perf tuning across the stack; make it reproducible. [Block C] Ship it: repo, architecture diagram, README and a demo — your flagship Data Engineering portfolio project.
units.demo: End-to-end data platform: ingestion → lakehouse → orchestration → data quality.

units.title: Phase 1 review
units.text: You've built the machine beneath the data and a full platform on top. Step back: what would you do differently, and which pieces will the ML and AI phases plug into?
units.mastery: Give the 3-minute architecture tour of your platform: how data flows from source to gold, and where quality, orchestration and cost are handled.

units.title: Vectors, matrices & operations
units.text:
Vectors as points/directions, matrices as linear maps; dot products and matrix multiply as composition of transforms — the language of ML.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — Essence of Linear Algebra (ch.1-4).
💻 Code: Implement vector/matrix ops in NumPy from the definitions and verify against np.dot.

units.title: Matrix decompositions: eigen & SVD
units.text:
Eigenvectors/values (directions a transform only scales) and SVD (any matrix = rotate-scale-rotate) — the engine behind PCA, recommenders and compression.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — eigenvectors; StatQuest — SVD/PCA.
💻 Code: Compute eigen-decomposition and SVD with NumPy; reconstruct a matrix from its top-k singular values.

units.title: Vector spaces, projections & norms
units.text:
Span, basis, linear independence, projections (least squares) and L1/L2 norms — geometry that underlies regression and regularization.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — Essence of Linear Algebra (span/basis/dot).
💻 Code: Project a vector onto a subspace and solve a least-squares fit via the normal equations.

units.title: PCA from linear algebra
units.text:
PCA is the eigen-decomposition of the covariance (or SVD of centered data); it finds the axes of maximum variance for dimensionality reduction.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — PCA step-by-step.
💻 Code: Implement PCA from scratch (center, covariance, eigen/SVD, project) and compare to sklearn.

units.title: NumPy for linear algebra
units.text:
Broadcasting, vectorized linear algebra (np.linalg), and why staying in NumPy instead of Python loops is 100x faster.
🎥 Watch: Jake VanderPlas — Python Data Science Handbook (NumPy).
💻 Code: Vectorize a from-scratch algorithm (e.g. a k-means step) using broadcasting; benchmark vs loops.

units.title: Implement PCA from scratch; compress images
units.text: [Block A] Build PCA from scratch (center, covariance/SVD, project, reconstruct) and validate against sklearn. [Block B] Apply it to image compression: reduce to k components, reconstruct, and plot explained-variance vs quality. [Block C] Write up the linear-algebra intuition with visuals — a clean portfolio notebook.

units.title: Linear-algebra intuition
units.text: Vectors/matrices, eigen/SVD, projections/norms and PCA are the geometric core of ML. Re-derive PCA from the covariance in your head.
units.mastery: What does SVD do geometrically, and why is PCA just an eigen/SVD problem on centered data?

units.title: Derivatives, gradients & the chain rule
units.text:
Derivatives as sensitivity, the gradient as the direction of steepest ascent, and the chain rule that makes backprop possible.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — Essence of Calculus (ch.1-4).
💻 Code: Implement numeric and analytic gradients for a small function and check they match.

units.title: Gradient descent & its variants
units.text:
Following the negative gradient to minimize loss; learning rate, batch vs stochastic vs mini-batch, momentum and Adam.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — gradient descent (Neural Networks ch.2); StatQuest — gradient descent.
💻 Code: Implement batch and mini-batch gradient descent for linear regression from scratch.

units.title: Convexity & Lagrange multipliers
units.text:
Convex problems have one global minimum (why linear/logistic regression are nice); Lagrange multipliers handle constrained optimization.
🎥 Watch: Search 'convex optimization intuition'; Khan Academy — Lagrange multipliers.
💻 Code: Minimize a convex function with gradient descent, verify the global optimum, and solve a simple constrained problem.

units.title: Backprop as the chain rule (preview)
units.text:
Backpropagation is just the chain rule applied over a computation graph — a preview you'll build for real in the AI phase.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — backpropagation; Andrej Karpathy — micrograd (intro).
💻 Code: Hand-derive gradients for a 2-layer function via the chain rule and verify them numerically.

units.title: Optimization in practice
units.text:
Learning-rate schedules, initialization, local minima vs saddle points, and diagnosing bad optimization.
🎥 Watch: Search 'optimization tricks deep learning'; Andrew Ng — optimization lectures.
💻 Code: Visualize gradient descent on a 2D loss surface with different learning rates.

units.title: Gradient-descent visualizer over loss landscapes
units.text: [Block A] Implement gradient descent (with momentum + Adam) from scratch on 2D test functions (bowl, saddle, Rosenbrock). [Block B] Animate the optimizer's path over contour plots; show how LR, momentum and the surface interact. [Block C] Extend it to fit a small model and visualize the loss dropping — a great intuition-building portfolio piece.

units.title: How models learn
units.text: Gradients, gradient descent, convexity and the chain rule are the machinery of every model that learns. Re-watch backprop with your visualizer open.
units.mastery: Why does gradient descent work, and what do momentum and Adam fix about plain SGD?

units.title: Probability & distributions
units.text:
Random variables, PMF/PDF, expectation/variance, and the key distributions (Bernoulli, binomial, normal, Poisson) you meet everywhere.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — probability & distributions; Khan Academy — probability.
💻 Code: Simulate distributions in NumPy, plot histograms vs the theoretical PDF, and estimate mean/variance.

units.title: Bayes & conditional probability
units.text:
Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, prior/likelihood/posterior, and the base-rate fallacy that fools everyone.
🎥 Watch: 3Blue1Brown — Bayes' theorem; StatQuest — Bayes.
💻 Code: Compute a posterior for a classic problem (medical test) and show how the base rate dominates.

units.title: Descriptive & inferential statistics
units.text:
Sampling, the central limit theorem, standard error, and going from a sample to a population claim.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — CLT and standard error; Khan Academy — inference.
💻 Code: Demonstrate the CLT by sampling means from a non-normal distribution and watching them go normal.

units.title: Hypothesis testing, CIs & p-values
units.text:
Null/alternative hypotheses, p-values (and what they are NOT), confidence intervals and t-tests.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — p-values, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals.
💻 Code: Run a t-test + bootstrap confidence interval on a real dataset and interpret the p-value correctly.

units.title: A/B testing & experimental design
units.text:
Designing experiments, power/sample size, and pitfalls (peeking, multiple comparisons) — the DS bread and butter.
🎥 Watch: Search 'A/B testing statistics'; StatQuest — power analysis.
💻 Code: Design and analyze an A/B test: compute the required sample size, then analyze simulated results.

units.title: A/B-test analysis toolkit + a simulation
units.text: [Block A] Build a reusable A/B toolkit: a sample-size/power calculator, t-test + bootstrap CIs, and effect-size reporting. [Block B] Run a Monte Carlo simulation showing false-positive rates under peeking and multiple comparisons. [Block C] Package + document it with a clear 'how to run a valid A/B test' guide — a standout portfolio piece for DS roles.

units.title: Reasoning under uncertainty
units.text: Distributions, Bayes, inference, hypothesis testing and A/B design are how you make honest claims from data. Re-read your p-value interpretation and get it exactly right.
units.mastery: What does a p-value actually mean (and not mean), and why does peeking at an A/B test inflate false positives?

units.title: NumPy deep: broadcasting & vectorization
units.text:
The ndarray, broadcasting rules, fancy indexing and vectorized thinking — the substrate under pandas and every ML library.
🎥 Watch: Jake VanderPlas — Python Data Science Handbook (NumPy); Keith Galli — NumPy.
💻 Code: Solve 10 array problems using only vectorized ops (no Python loops).

units.title: Pandas mastery: groupby, merge, reshape
units.text:
Indexing/selection, groupby-apply, joins/merges, pivot/melt and time-based ops — the daily driver of data work.
🎥 Watch: Wes McKinney — Python for Data Analysis; Keith Galli — pandas.
💻 Code: Do a full wrangle: load messy data, groupby-aggregate, merge sources, pivot to a report.

units.title: EDA methodology
units.text:
A disciplined EDA loop: shape/types, distributions, missingness, correlations, outliers, and forming hypotheses before modeling.
🎥 Watch: Search 'exploratory data analysis methodology'; strong Kaggle EDA notebooks.
💻 Code: Run a structured EDA on a real dataset and write down 5 hypotheses it surfaces.

units.title: Cleaning, missing data & outliers
units.text:
Missing-data mechanisms (MCAR/MAR/MNAR), imputation strategies, outlier detection, and how cleaning choices bias results.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — missing data; search 'handling missing data imputation'.
💻 Code: Handle missing values three ways (drop, mean, model-based) and compare the downstream impact.

units.title: Visualization: matplotlib, seaborn, plotly
units.text:
Choosing the right chart, matplotlib fundamentals, seaborn for stats plots, plotly for interactivity, and honest visualization.
🎥 Watch: Corey Schafer — matplotlib; the seaborn docs.
💻 Code: Build a small dashboard of 4 well-chosen charts that tell a story about your dataset.

units.title: End-to-end EDA report on a real dataset
units.text: [Block A] Pick a rich real dataset; do a rigorous EDA — quality, distributions, relationships, outliers. [Block B] Clean it (documented decisions on missing/outliers) and engineer a few features. [Block C] Produce a polished notebook/report with clear visuals and findings — a portfolio data-analyst showcase.

units.title: Letting the data speak
units.text: NumPy, pandas, EDA method, cleaning and visualization turn raw files into understanding — the step before any model. Re-read your EDA's conclusions.
units.mastery: What's your EDA checklist before modeling, and how can a naive missing-data fix bias your results?

units.title: The ML framework: bias-variance
units.text:
Train/validation/test splits, generalization, overfitting/underfitting, and the bias-variance tradeoff that governs everything.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — bias/variance; Andrew Ng — Machine Learning Specialization (course 1).
💻 Code: Fit models of increasing complexity and plot train vs validation error to see the tradeoff.

units.title: Linear regression from scratch
units.text:
The model, the loss (MSE), the closed-form normal equation, and gradient descent — regression from first principles.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — linear regression; Andrew Ng — linear regression.
💻 Code: Implement linear regression from scratch (normal equation and gradient descent) and match sklearn.

units.title: Logistic regression & classification
units.text:
The sigmoid, log-loss, decision boundaries, and why it's classification despite the name.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — logistic regression; Andrew Ng — classification.
💻 Code: Implement logistic regression from scratch with gradient descent on a binary dataset.

units.title: Regularization: L1/L2 & elastic net
units.text:
Ridge (L2), Lasso (L1, sparsity/feature selection) and elastic net; how the penalty trades bias for lower variance.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — ridge, lasso, elastic net.
💻 Code: Add L1 and L2 penalties to your regression; watch coefficients shrink and features drop out.

units.title: The sklearn API & pipelines
units.text:
fit/predict/transform, Pipeline + ColumnTransformer, cross-validation, and avoiding leakage by preprocessing inside the pipeline.
🎥 Watch: Search 'sklearn pipeline tutorial'; the sklearn user guide.
💻 Code: Build a leak-free sklearn Pipeline (impute -> scale -> encode -> model) with cross-validation.

units.title: Linear & logistic regression from scratch
units.text: [Block A] Implement linear and logistic regression from scratch (loss, gradients, training loop, regularization). [Block B] Validate against sklearn on real datasets; add L1/L2 and plot the effect. [Block C] Write it up as a 'ML from first principles' notebook — it proves you understand what the library hides.

units.title: The supervised-learning core
units.text: The train/val/test frame, bias-variance, the two workhorse models, regularization and the sklearn workflow are the foundation of applied ML. Re-derive the logistic gradient.
units.mastery: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff with a concrete overfit example, and what L1 does that L2 doesn't.

units.title: Decision trees
units.text:
Recursive splits on impurity (Gini/entropy), how trees overfit, and pruning/depth control.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — decision trees.
💻 Code: Fit a decision tree, visualize it, and show how max_depth controls overfitting.

units.title: Bagging & random forests
units.text:
Bootstrap aggregating to reduce variance; random forests add feature randomness for decorrelated trees.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — random forests and bagging.
💻 Code: Build a random forest, compare it to a single tree, and inspect out-of-bag error.

units.title: Gradient boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM)
units.text:
Boosting fits trees to residuals sequentially; XGBoost/LightGBM are the tabular workhorses that win competitions.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — gradient boost and XGBoost.
💻 Code: Train XGBoost and LightGBM on a tabular problem; tune key params and beat the random forest.

units.title: Feature importance & SHAP
units.text:
Impurity vs permutation importance (and their traps), and SHAP for consistent per-prediction explanations.
🎥 Watch: Search 'SHAP values explained'; StatQuest — SHAP.
💻 Code: Compute SHAP values for your boosted model and explain a few individual predictions.

units.title: Hyperparameter tuning
units.text:
Grid vs random vs Bayesian search (Optuna), cross-validated tuning, and not overfitting the validation set.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Optuna tutorial' and 'hyperparameter tuning strategies'.
💻 Code: Tune your XGBoost model with Optuna + cross-validation and report the honest gain.

units.title: Kaggle-style win with gradient boosting
units.text: [Block A] Take a real tabular problem (a Kaggle dataset) and build a strong baseline with proper CV. [Block B] Engineer features and tune XGBoost/LightGBM with Optuna; add SHAP explanations. [Block C] Write up the approach + a leaderboard-style result — a portfolio piece that shows applied ML judgment.

units.title: Ensembles in practice
units.text: Trees, bagging/forests, boosting, importance/SHAP and tuning are the tabular-ML toolkit that wins in practice. Re-read your SHAP explanations.
units.mastery: Why does bagging reduce variance while boosting reduces bias, and what makes gradient boosting so strong on tabular data?

units.title: SVMs & kernels
units.text:
Maximum-margin classifiers and the kernel trick for non-linear boundaries without explicit high-dim features.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — SVMs and kernels.
💻 Code: Train an SVM with linear and RBF kernels; visualize the decision boundary and margins.

units.title: kNN & Naive Bayes
units.text:
Instance-based kNN (lazy, distance-driven) and Naive Bayes (fast, probabilistic, strong on text).
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — kNN and Naive Bayes.
💻 Code: Implement kNN from scratch and use Naive Bayes for a text-classification baseline.

units.title: Clustering: k-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical
units.text:
Unsupervised grouping: k-means (centroids), DBSCAN (density, finds noise), hierarchical (dendrograms) — and picking k.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — k-means and hierarchical clustering.
💻 Code: Cluster a dataset three ways; compare and use the elbow/silhouette to pick k.

units.title: Dimensionality reduction: t-SNE & UMAP
units.text:
Non-linear embeddings for visualization (t-SNE, UMAP) vs PCA, and how to read (and misread) these plots.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — t-SNE; search 'UMAP explained'.
💻 Code: Embed a high-dim dataset with PCA, t-SNE and UMAP; compare the 2D structure.

units.title: Anomaly detection
units.text:
Statistical, isolation-forest and density-based anomaly detection, and the imbalance/evaluation challenge.
🎥 Watch: Search 'anomaly detection isolation forest'.
💻 Code: Detect anomalies with an isolation forest and evaluate with precision@k on a labeled set.

units.title: Customer-segmentation (unsupervised) project
units.text: [Block A] Take a real customer/behavior dataset; engineer features and pick a clustering approach with justification. [Block B] Cluster, choose k rigorously (elbow/silhouette), profile each segment, and visualize with UMAP. [Block C] Turn segments into a business narrative + recommendations — a portfolio piece that shows unsupervised judgment.

units.title: The algorithm zoo
units.text: SVMs/kernels, kNN/Naive Bayes, clustering, dimensionality reduction and anomaly detection round out classical ML. Re-read your t-SNE plot critically.
units.mastery: When would you reach for DBSCAN over k-means, and why can a t-SNE plot mislead you?

units.title: Feature-engineering techniques
units.text:
Transformations, interactions, binning and aggregations — and why features often matter more than the model.
🎥 Watch: Search 'feature engineering for machine learning'; the Kaggle Feature Engineering course.
💻 Code: Engineer 10 features for a tabular problem and measure each one's marginal lift.

units.title: Categorical encoding & embeddings
units.text:
One-hot, ordinal, target/mean encoding (with leakage care), and learned embeddings for high-cardinality categories.
🎥 Watch: Search 'categorical encoding techniques' and 'target encoding leakage'.
💻 Code: Compare one-hot vs target encoding (done inside CV to avoid leakage) on a high-cardinality feature.

units.title: Scaling & transformations
units.text:
Standardization vs min-max, log/Box-Cox for skew, and when scaling matters (SVM/kNN/NN) vs not (trees).
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — normalization; search 'feature scaling when to use'.
💻 Code: Show how scaling changes kNN/SVM but not a tree, and apply a log transform to a skewed feature.

units.title: Time-series features
units.text:
Lags, rolling windows, date/calendar features, and avoiding leakage from the future in temporal data.
🎥 Watch: Search 'time series feature engineering'.
💻 Code: Build lag + rolling features for a time series with a strict no-future-leakage split.

units.title: Feature stores (Feast)
units.text:
Why feature stores exist (training/serving consistency, reuse, point-in-time correctness) and how Feast works.
🎥 Watch: Search 'feature store explained'; the Feast quickstart.
💻 Code: Define a couple of features in Feast, materialize them, and fetch a point-in-time training set.

units.title: Feature pipeline + a feature store
units.text: [Block A] Build a reusable feature pipeline (transformations, encoding, scaling) as sklearn transformers, leak-free. [Block B] Register features in Feast with point-in-time correctness; serve them for training and inference. [Block C] Document the training/serving-skew problem the feature store solves — a strong MLOps-adjacent portfolio piece.

units.title: Features make or break models
units.text: Techniques, encoding, scaling, time-series features and feature stores are where most model performance actually comes from. Re-check one feature for leakage.
units.mastery: What is training/serving skew, and how does target encoding leak if you're not careful?

units.title: Metrics: classification, regression, ranking
units.text:
Accuracy's traps, precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC vs PR-AUC, regression metrics (RMSE/MAE/R2), and ranking metrics (NDCG).
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — confusion matrix, ROC/AUC, precision/recall.
💻 Code: Compute the full metric suite for a model and explain which metric fits the business goal.

units.title: Cross-validation strategies
units.text:
k-fold, stratified, group and time-series CV — matching the split to the data for an honest estimate.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — cross validation; search 'time series cross validation'.
💻 Code: Compare naive k-fold vs grouped/time-series CV on data with groups/time; show the leakage gap.

units.title: ROC/PR curves & calibration
units.text:
Threshold choice via ROC/PR, and probability calibration (reliability curves, Platt/isotonic) so scores mean something.
🎥 Watch: StatQuest — ROC/AUC; search 'model calibration explained'.
💻 Code: Plot ROC + PR curves, pick a threshold for a cost tradeoff, and calibrate the probabilities.

units.title: Handling class imbalance
units.text:
Resampling (SMOTE), class weights, threshold moving, and why accuracy lies on imbalanced data.
🎥 Watch: Search 'handling imbalanced data' and 'SMOTE explained'.
💻 Code: Take an imbalanced problem; compare class weights, SMOTE and threshold tuning by PR-AUC.

units.title: Interpretability
units.text:
Global (feature importance, PDP) vs local (SHAP, LIME) explanations, and communicating model behavior to stakeholders.
🎥 Watch: Search 'SHAP vs LIME' and 'partial dependence plots'.
💻 Code: Explain your model globally (PDP) and locally (SHAP), then write a one-paragraph stakeholder summary.

units.title: Evaluation + interpretability toolkit
units.text: [Block A] Build a reusable evaluation module: the metric suite, the right CV, ROC/PR + calibration plots. [Block B] Add interpretability: PDPs, SHAP, and an imbalance-aware threshold selector. [Block C] Run it on a real model and produce a model card — a portfolio piece that shows rigor, not just accuracy.

units.title: Trusting your metrics
units.text: Metrics, CV, calibration, imbalance handling and interpretability are how you know a model is actually good. Re-read your model card.
units.mastery: Why can accuracy be 99% and useless, and when is PR-AUC the honest metric over ROC-AUC?

units.title: TS concepts: stationarity & autocorrelation
units.text:
Trend/seasonality/noise decomposition, stationarity, and autocorrelation (ACF/PACF) — the vocabulary of time series.
🎥 Watch: Search 'time series analysis stationarity ACF PACF'.
💻 Code: Decompose a series, test stationarity (ADF), and plot ACF/PACF.

units.title: Classical: ARIMA & ETS
units.text:
AR, MA, ARIMA and exponential smoothing (ETS); when classical models still beat ML on small clean series.
🎥 Watch: Search 'ARIMA explained' and 'exponential smoothing'.
💻 Code: Fit ARIMA and ETS to a series, diagnose residuals, and forecast with intervals.

units.title: Prophet & modern methods
units.text:
Prophet's decomposable model, and ML approaches (gradient boosting on lag features) for complex series.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Facebook Prophet tutorial'.
💻 Code: Forecast the same series with Prophet and a gradient-boosting-on-lags model, then compare.

units.title: Feature-based forecasting
units.text:
Reframing forecasting as supervised learning with lag/rolling/calendar features, and multi-step strategies.
🎥 Watch: Search 'time series forecasting as supervised learning'.
💻 Code: Build a feature-based forecaster with proper temporal CV and compare it to ARIMA.

units.title: Evaluation & backtesting
units.text:
Rolling-origin backtesting, horizon-aware metrics (MAPE/sMAPE/MASE), and why a random split is wrong here.
🎥 Watch: Search 'time series cross validation backtesting'.
💻 Code: Backtest your models with rolling-origin evaluation and report horizon-wise error.

units.title: Demand / energy forecasting with backtesting
units.text: [Block A] Pick a real forecasting problem (demand, energy, traffic); EDA + decomposition + features. [Block B] Build classical (ARIMA/Prophet) and ML (boosting-on-lags) forecasters; backtest with rolling origin. [Block C] Report which wins by horizon with proper metrics + intervals — a rigorous forecasting portfolio piece.

units.title: Predicting the future
units.text: Stationarity/autocorrelation, classical models, Prophet/ML, feature-based framing and backtesting are the forecasting toolkit. Re-read your backtest for leakage.
units.mastery: Why is a random train/test split wrong for time series, and how does rolling-origin backtesting fix it?

units.title: Collaborative filtering
units.text:
User-user and item-item CF from the interaction matrix; the 'people like you also liked' intuition.
🎥 Watch: Search 'collaborative filtering explained'; Andrew Ng — recommenders.
💻 Code: Implement item-item collaborative filtering from a ratings matrix.

units.title: Matrix factorization
units.text:
Learning latent user/item factors (SVD-style, ALS) to fill the sparse matrix — the classic recsys workhorse.
🎥 Watch: Search 'matrix factorization recommender systems'.
💻 Code: Implement matrix factorization with gradient descent on a ratings dataset.

units.title: Content-based & hybrid
units.text:
Using item features (and embeddings) for cold-start, and hybrid systems that blend CF + content.
🎥 Watch: Search 'content based vs collaborative filtering hybrid'.
💻 Code: Add a content-based model and blend it with your CF into a hybrid recommender.

units.title: Implicit feedback & ranking
units.text:
Clicks/views (implicit) vs ratings, ranking losses (BPR), and the top-N recommendation framing.
🎥 Watch: Search 'implicit feedback recommender BPR'.
💻 Code: Train an implicit-feedback ranker and generate top-N recommendations.

units.title: Recommender evaluation
units.text:
Offline metrics (precision@k, recall@k, NDCG, MAP), the offline/online gap, and coverage/diversity.
🎥 Watch: Search 'recommender system evaluation metrics'.
💻 Code: Evaluate your recommenders with precision@k + NDCG and compare them fairly.

units.title: End-to-end recommender system
units.text: [Block A] Pick a real interactions dataset (MovieLens etc.) and build CF + matrix-factorization baselines. [Block B] Add content features for cold-start and a hybrid ranker for implicit feedback. [Block C] Evaluate with ranking metrics and serve top-N via a small API — a portfolio recsys project.
units.demo: Production recommender system (collaborative + matrix factorization + hybrid), served via API.

units.title: Systems that personalize
units.text: Collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, content/hybrid, implicit ranking and evaluation are the recommender toolkit. Re-read your offline-vs-online caveat.
units.mastery: How does matrix factorization fill a sparse ratings matrix, and why can offline metrics mislead you about a live recommender?

units.title: ML system design
units.text:
The full ML lifecycle (data -> features -> train -> serve -> monitor), and why more than 90% of the work isn't the model.
🎥 Watch: Chip Huyen — Designing ML Systems (overview); Made With ML.
💻 Code: Draw the end-to-end architecture for an ML system you'll build, labeling every component.

units.title: Experiment tracking (MLflow, W&B)
units.text:
Tracking params/metrics/artifacts for reproducibility and comparison instead of losing results in notebooks.
🎥 Watch: MLflow quickstart; Weights & Biases tutorials.
💻 Code: Instrument a training script with MLflow (params, metrics, model) and compare runs in the UI.

units.title: Model registry & versioning
units.text:
Registering models with stages (staging/production), versioning, and promoting the right model to serving.
🎥 Watch: MLflow Model Registry docs.
💻 Code: Register your model, version it, and promote a version to 'production' via the registry.

units.title: Reproducible ML pipelines
units.text:
Turning notebooks into reproducible pipelines (scripts, configs, seeds, environments) so results are rebuildable.
🎥 Watch: Made With ML — reproducibility; search 'reproducible ML pipeline'.
💻 Code: Refactor a notebook into a config-driven, seeded training pipeline that runs end to end.

units.title: Data & model versioning (DVC)
units.text:
Versioning datasets and models alongside code with DVC, so an experiment is fully reconstructable.
🎥 Watch: DVC docs/tutorial.
💻 Code: Version a dataset + model with DVC and reproduce a past experiment from a git+dvc checkout.

units.title: MLflow-tracked training pipeline
units.text: [Block A] Build a reproducible, config-driven training pipeline (data -> features -> train -> evaluate). [Block B] Instrument it with MLflow (params/metrics/artifacts) + DVC data versioning, and register the best model. [Block C] Document how to reproduce any run from git + dvc — a portfolio MLOps foundation piece.

units.title: From notebook to system
units.text: System design, experiment tracking, registry/versioning, reproducibility and DVC turn ad-hoc modeling into engineering. Reproduce an old run to prove it works.
units.mastery: What makes an ML experiment reproducible, and what does a model registry give you that a folder of pickles doesn't?

units.title: Serving (FastAPI, BentoML)
units.text:
Wrapping a model in an API, request/response schemas, and packaging with BentoML for standardized serving.
🎥 Watch: Search 'FastAPI ML model serving'; the BentoML docs.
💻 Code: Serve your model behind a FastAPI endpoint with a typed request/response and validation.

units.title: Batch vs online inference
units.text:
Precomputed batch predictions vs low-latency online inference, and the latency/cost/freshness tradeoffs.
🎥 Watch: Chip Huyen — batch vs online; search 'batch vs online inference'.
💻 Code: Implement both a batch scoring job and an online endpoint for the same model; compare latency.

units.title: Monitoring: drift & performance
units.text:
Data drift, concept drift, and monitoring live performance/latency — models decay silently without it.
🎥 Watch: Search 'ML model monitoring data drift'; the Evidently AI docs.
💻 Code: Add drift detection (e.g. Evidently) + latency/throughput metrics to your service.

units.title: Shadow & A/B deployment
units.text:
Rolling out models safely: shadow (mirror traffic), canary, and A/B testing model versions in production.
🎥 Watch: Search 'shadow deployment canary ML'.
💻 Code: Add a shadow-mode path that scores with a new model without affecting responses; log the comparison.

units.title: CI/CD for ML
units.text:
Automated testing, model-validation gates, and deployment pipelines (CML/GitHub Actions) for models.
🎥 Watch: Search 'CI/CD for machine learning'; Made With ML — CI/CD.
💻 Code: Wire a CI pipeline that tests, validates the model against a threshold, and deploys on pass.

units.title: Deploy a model as an API with monitoring
units.text: [Block A] Serve your model via FastAPI/BentoML with schemas, containerized. [Block B] Add monitoring: drift detection, latency/throughput metrics and alerting, plus a shadow-mode path. [Block C] Wire CI/CD with a model-validation gate and deploy — a flagship MLOps portfolio project.
units.demo: ML model served as an API with drift monitoring and CI/CD.

units.title: Keeping models alive
units.text: Serving, batch vs online, monitoring, safe rollout and CI/CD are what keep a model useful after launch. Re-check that your drift monitor fires.
units.mastery: How would you detect that a live model has silently degraded, and what's your safe path to ship a replacement?

units.title: Designing ML systems (a framework)
units.text:
Framing an ML problem: objective, constraints, data, baseline, metrics, and the design-doc discipline.
🎥 Watch: Chip Huyen — Designing ML Systems; search 'ML system design interview'.
💻 Code: Write a full ML design doc for a realistic problem (fraud/recsys/churn).

units.title: Scaling training: distributed & data-parallel
units.text:
Data vs model parallelism, and scaling training across GPUs/nodes when data or models don't fit.
🎥 Watch: Search 'distributed training data parallel explained'.
💻 Code: Run a data-parallel training job (PyTorch DDP or Spark ML) and measure the scaling.

units.title: Feature/label pipelines at scale
units.text:
Building training data at scale, point-in-time correctness, and label generation / weak supervision.
🎥 Watch: Chip Huyen — training data; search 'weak supervision Snorkel'.
💻 Code: Build a point-in-time-correct training set from event logs (no future leakage).

units.title: Cost & latency tradeoffs
units.text:
Model size vs accuracy vs latency vs cost, caching predictions, and choosing the cheapest thing that works.
🎥 Watch: Search 'ML inference cost optimization'.
💻 Code: Profile inference cost/latency and cut it (quantization/caching/simpler model) within an accuracy budget.

units.title: Case studies: fraud, recsys
units.text:
Reading real ML system designs (feature pipelines, serving, feedback loops) to build pattern intuition.
🎥 Watch: Search 'Uber Michelangelo' and 'Netflix recommendations system design'.
💻 Code: Reverse-engineer a public ML system design into a diagram + tradeoff notes.

units.title: ML system-design doc + a prototype
units.text: [Block A] Choose a realistic problem and write a full system-design doc (objective, data, features, model, serving, monitoring, tradeoffs).
